claude-bridge/claude-fable-5.character: Advisory: The advisor's own session model and the default planner. The advisor session runs at medium; planner nodes run at high. Shares the Anthropic session allowance — generally avoid assigning checking, review, reduction, browser verification, or implementation. When Anthropic capacity is reached, planning falls back to Sol at high and the advisor session switches to Sol.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol.character: Advisory: Tenacious high-intelligence workhorse for long or difficult backend, data, and service implementation. Use medium for token-efficient fresh-context review, synthesis, bounded investigation, ambiguous browser verification, and bounded implementation that still needs material local judgment. Planning fallback, advisor use, and substantial builds remain high. Frontend implementation otherwise routes to Opus or Grok by UX scope. Sol medium is also the adversarial checker for schema, auth, security, money, and data boundaries. For builds, high is enough for nearly all work; escalate to xhigh or max only for genuinely difficult debugging. Prefer Luna, not Sol medium, when an execution packet has already locked the approach and material decisions.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna.character: Advisory: Extremely cheap; the procedural-tier workhorse for scouting, mechanical chores, routine mid-phase checks, repair verification, test-harness findings, browser verification, and implementation from a locked execution packet. The packet must fix the material approach, bound the surface, and name deterministic anchors. Luna owns ordinary local code choices but stops and escalates rather than deciding product, architecture, schema, migration, auth, fallback, destructive behavior, or external effects. 272K window. Generally avoid adversarial-tier checking and decision-bearing implementation. Recommended reasoning is max.

claude-bridge/claude-opus-5.character: Advisory: Reserve for genuinely new or greenfield UX/frontend implementation when Anthropic session capacity is healthy, preferably with frontend-design loaded. Runs at medium reasoning. Grok is the automatic UX fallback when capacity is tight or an Opus launch hits a capacity limit. Not recommended for existing-UX tweaks, checking, review, reduction, planning, or backend.

cursor/grok-4.6.character: Advisory: High-efficiency generalist at high reasoning. Preferred for research, bounded backend implementation, mixed-stack work, substantial changes to an existing UX, and UX implementation when Opus would consume scarce Anthropic/Fable session capacity. New UX uses Opus while capacity is healthy, then Grok automatically. Load frontend-design for UX work. 200K window — keep packets bounded and split oversized work. Preserve Cursor catalog fast-mode default. This guide recommends Cursor only as cursor/grok-4.6.
